summary:
Abstract
The Ecosystem Viewer & OLAP Telemetry Platform is an interactive, responsive 3D and 2D web observatory built with Flutter Web that pairs immersive biome visualization with real-time Earth observation telemetry and containerized analytical pipelines. Users navigate global environments—including Jungle Forests, Ocean Floors, Cloud Forests, and Seagrass Meadows—by inspecting interactive .glb 3D models layered over transparent multi-frame sprite-sheet animations. Concurrently, the platform aggregates multi-stream satellite and meteorological telemetry via asynchronous requests (Future.wait), uniting Open-Meteo live forecasts, Parallel.ai search context, and dedicated NASA Earth science modules: Drought (Soil moisture anomaly by region derived from NASA SMAP), Precipitation (Global precipitation anomaly by year retrieved from NASA GPM / GPCP), and Vegetation (Vegetation index trend by continent retrieved from NASA MODIS). High-throughput analytical metrics are ingested into a containerized ClickHouse columnar OLAP backend and surfaced through a frosted glassmorphism Grafana MCP heads-up display (HUD). Complete with local WebAssembly SQLite persistence, a 10-chart data visualization engine, six-language RTL/LTR localization, and automated per-page PDF/RSS publishing, the platform makes planetary climate anomalies accessible, interactive, and actionable in any modern browser.
details:
Overview

The platform bridges spatial biome immersion with scientific data observability inside a single multi-page Flutter Web application:

  • 3D & 2.5D Ecosystem Exploration: Users switch dynamically between global biomes (ecosystems.dart). Each scene renders interactive 3D .glb models via model_viewer_plus layered in front of custom-painted, multi-frame transparent sprite-sheet animations (sprite_sheet_animator.dart), providing atmospheric motion with low GPU overhead.
    • NASA GISS (Climate Telemetry): Integrates data from the DataHub Core Global Temperature / GISS Maintenance Report to monitor Global surface temperature and precipitation anomaly updates.
    • NASA SMAP (Drought): Fetches soil moisture retrieval models to track Soil moisture anomaly by region.
    • NASA GPM / GPCP (Precipitation): Retrieves rainfall datasets to visualize Global precipitation anomaly by year.
    • NASA MODIS (Vegetation): Pulls surface reflectance products to monitor Vegetation index trend by continent.
  • Concurrent OLAP & AI Pipeline: Using dio and Future.wait (olap_service.dart), the client executes parallel data fetches combining live coordinate-based weather from Open-Meteo and AI-augmented ecological summaries from Parallel.ai. Analytical events are logged to a containerized ClickHouse columnar database (schema.sql) and rendered in a translucent glassmorphism HUD (grafana_mcp_dashboard_widget.dart) connected to a Grafana MCP server.
  • Client-Side Persistence & Publishing: Local SQLite (sqflite_common_ffi_web) stores timestamped field notes (timeago), salted-hash admin credentials, and service bookings—which immediately render across ten interactive chart types (charts_page.dart). Every page also auto-generates downloadable PDFs, RSS 2.0 feeds, social share links, and a sitemap.xml.

Key Benefits

  • Unified Visual & Quantitative Context: Eliminates the disconnect between raw climate spreadsheets and physical habitats by overlaying real-time meteorological and NASA anomaly metrics directly onto interactive 3D ecosystems.
  • Non-Blocking Web Concurrency: Asynchronous multi-stream fetching (Future.wait) paired with columnar OLAP storage ensures high-frequency telemetry updates never stall 3D model interaction or sprite animations.
  • Zero-Latency Local Analytics: Browser-native SQLite allows researchers, students, and developers to record notes, manage schedules, and generate 10-chart visual breakdowns locally without round-trip server delays.
  • Global Accessibility & Open Distribution: Native six-language support (English, Español, Deutsch, हिन्दी, العربية with right-to-left rendering, and Français) and automated PDF/RSS generation make findings immediately shareable across international communities.

Intended Impact

The project is designed to democratize access to NASA Earth science data, climate literacy, and ecological monitoring. By translating complex multi-decadal datasets—such as global rainfall anomalies, continental vegetation shifts, and regional soil moisture deficits—into intuitive 3D environments and glassmorphic dashboards, the platform empowers students, educators, conservationists, and citizen scientists to explore how global climate anomalies affect specific biomes. Furthermore, its modular page registry and containerized telemetry stack provide an open, reproducible architectural blueprint for web-based scientific visualization.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Coding Languages: Dart, SQL (schema.sql), HTML5/JavaScript (web/index.html & Model Viewer integration), YAML (docker-compose.yml).
  • Frontend Framework & UI: Flutter Web (v3.0+), model_viewer_plus (3D .glb rendering), custom CustomPainter widgets (glassmorphism HUD & multi-frame sprite animator), font_awesome_flutter.
  • Earth Observation & Telemetry APIs: NASA SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive), NASA GPM / GPCP (Global Precipitation Measurement / Global Precipitation Climatology Project), NASA MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer), Open-Meteo API, Parallel.ai Search API.
  • Backend, Database & Observability: ClickHouse (columnar OLAP database), Grafana Cloud & Grafana MCP Server, Docker & Docker Compose.
  • Client Storage & Publishing: sqflite / sqflite_common_ffi_web (WebAssembly SQLite), custom per-page PDF and RSS 2.0 generation engines (rss_pdf_service.dart).
  • Hardware & Target Environment: Developed on standard multi-core workstations capable of running containerized Docker clusters and tested across modern WebGL/Wasm-enabled desktop and mobile browsers.

How the Project Is Creative

  • Hybrid 2.5D/3D Rendering Architecture: Rather than relying solely on heavy 3D scene graphs that tax browser memory, the custom SpriteSheetAnimator maps transparent multi-frame 2D sprite sheets (sprite-01.png to sprite--07.png) directly behind interactive .glb models—creating living atmospheric depth (drifting mist, underwater currents, canopy motion) while keeping frame rates smooth on web clients.
  • Aerospace-Inspired Glassmorphism HUD: Every view shares a unified PageShell featuring a live coordinate clock, breadcrumb navigation, dynamic QR code handoff, and a translucent frosted-glass Grafana MCP overlay that evokes scientific field instrumentation.
  • Interactive Data Storytelling Engine: User entries from the coding/research agenda are automatically transformed into ten distinct chart formats—including 3D columns, word clouds, flowcharts, multi-axis plots, and bubble charts—turning routine scheduling logs into an exploratory visual sandbox.

Factors Our Team Considered

  • Browser Wasm & SQLite Initialization: Running relational SQLite databases inside Flutter Web requires specific WebAssembly worker binaries (sqflite_common_ffi_web:setup) in web/ so database-backed pages (Notes, Charts, Agenda, Admin) load reliably without hanging.
  • Internationalization & Bidirectional Layout: Merging six languages into a single localization delegate (app_strings.dart) required careful responsive layout testing so breadcrumbs, glassmorphic cards, and media carousels mirror cleanly when switching to Arabic right-to-left (RTL) mode.
  • Single Source of Truth Maintainability: Engineering pages_registry.dart as the central definition for navigation drawers, PDF exports, RSS 2.0 feeds, and sitemap.xml ensured that adding new NASA telemetry pages (Drought, Precipitation, Vegetation) automatically propagated across every publishing and navigation surface without route drift.
  • Performance vs. Media Richness: Balancing 3D .glb assets, seven autoplaying muted local videos, Vimeo embeds, and concurrent API telemetry streams required strict asynchronous stream isolation and responsive grid scaling (LayoutBuilder) across mobile and desktop viewports.
